---
title: "🚦 Mission 0: Are you R Ready?"
---

::: {.mission-meta}
⏱️ About 2 minutes · no coding yet
:::

This isn't a test — there's no score to fail. It's just a quick way to see which of the next missions matter most for you. If you've never touched R before, expect to answer "not really" a lot, and that's exactly the point of this whole pre-course.

Read each statement. Be honest, not aspirational.

- [ ] **1. I have R *and* RStudio installed, and RStudio opens without an error.**
  *(Not R alone — you need both. R is the engine, RStudio is the dashboard.)*
- [ ] **2. I know what an "RStudio Project" is, and I've created one before.**
- [ ] **3. If someone asked "what's your current working directory?", I could answer without googling it.**
- [ ] **4. I know roughly what `<-`, `()`, and `$` each do in R.**
- [ ] **5. When R shows me a red error message, my first reaction is to read it, not to panic.**

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## How to read your results
Every unchecked box points straight at a mission:

| Unchecked | Go to |
|---|---|
| 1 | Install R and RStudio first — see your course welcome email, or ask us before continuing here. |
| 2 | [Mission 1 — Give your analysis a home](01-projects.qmd) |
| 3 | [Mission 2 — Help R find your files](02-paths.qmd) |
| 4 | [Mission 3 — Learn R's language](03-language.qmd) |
| 5 | [Mission 4 — Break R on purpose](04-errors.qmd) |

Checked everything? Great — skim the missions anyway, then jump straight to the [final challenge](06-final-challenge.qmd) to confirm your setup actually works end to end.
:::
